exteriorDecor.comment: === market stalls along the lower lane ===

animals.name: Floss
dialogue: *a lean farm dog circles you once, then sits, ears pricked*
*woof!*

animals.name: Mouser
dialogue: *a barn cat regards you from atop a hay bale*
*mrrp.*

animals.name: The Pond Duck
dialogue: *a fat white duck paddles a slow circuit of the pond*

npcs.name: Elder Maeve
dialogue: Harrowfield feeds half the kingdom and gets thanked by none of it. Sit a while; you're thanked here.
The scarecrows have been... moving. Pip says I imagine it. Pip didn't grow up here.
Stay for the harvest supper if you can. We owe travellers more kindness than we used to show.

npcs.name: Farmhand Pip
dialogue: Sowing, hoeing, mowing. The fields don't care what day it is.
Three seed-grain sacks have gone missing. Maeve will have my ears if they're not found.
The scarecrow moved again last night. I'm not paid enough to ask it why.

npcs.name: Miller Rook
dialogue: Flour, meal, and gossip — ground fresh daily.
The road south to the capital used to be safe. Now even the king's road has tolls of the unofficial kind.
Bring me grain and the stones will sing. Bread prices in Crownhaven would make you weep.

npcs.name: Shepherd Nan
dialogue: A good fence and a good dog — that's the whole of shepherding, and the dog does most of it.
Floss keeps the flock, but she can't mend a fence. The ewes are through the gap again.
Wool to the market, mutton never if I can help it. I get attached, see.

npcs.name: Baker Tovi
dialogue: Flour in, loaves out, and the whole village smells of breakfast by dawn.
Rook's flour, Maeve's blessing, my oven. Harrowfield runs on bread, traveller.
Bring me what I need and I'll see the supper tables never go bare.

npcs.name: Lark
dialogue: Rook grinds the grain; I keep the cottage from grinding us down.
Wash day and the linens have gone clean over the hedge in this wind. Honestly.
Mind the lane — the cart ruts'll have your ankle if the mud doesn't.

npcs.name: Pedlar Quill
dialogue: Grain, wool, eggs, cheese — if Harrowfield grows it, I find it a buyer.
Ravenwatch pays well for good country produce. Getting a cart there unrobbed is the trick.
Buy in the field, sell at the gate. That's the whole of trade, friend.

npcs.name: Sister Bell
dialogue: The chapel's small, but it fills to the rafters every harvest-tide.
We bless the first sheaf and the last loaf. The fields seem to listen.
Quiet hands and full barns. That's all the sermon Harrowfield needs.

npcs.name: Little Bram
dialogue: I'm not lost! The FIELD'S lost. I know exactly where I am. Mostly.
I lost my things running from the moving scarecrow. It WAS moving. I saw it!
When I grow up I'm going to drive the cart all the way to Ravenwatch. And back. Probably.

reactions.text: A patch of white wildflowers growing by the field's edge.
Pink flowers growing wild among the crop rows.
A cluster of blue flowers, swaying in the field wind.
Wedged between the chapel wall and the village hall, a small scrap of paper is tucked out of the wind.

collectible.name: Torn Hymnal Page
collectible.desc: A page torn from a chapel hymnal, the ink smudged with rain.
collectible.lore: Sister Bell would recognize the hand — one of the harvest blessing verses, with a line scratched out and rewritten: 'watch the fields, watch what walks them.'

reactions.message: You found a torn page from a hymnal.

reactions.text: Caught in the straw between the barn and the windmill, something small and metal glints.

collectible.name: Straw-Stuffed Button
collectible.desc: A plain button, still trailing a bit of straw and thread.
collectible.lore: Pip swears the scarecrows have been moving. This button looks like it came off one of their coats — and it's warm, somehow, though it's been lying in the dirt.

reactions.message: You found a strange warm button. The scarecrows might be missing it.

reactions.text: Half-buried near the mill lane, a small brass gear turns faintly on its own, though nothing drives it.

collectible.name: Ever-Turning Gear
collectible.desc: A small brass gear that never quite stops spinning.
collectible.lore: Miller Rook would swear his windmill's never lost a gear — and yet here one is, still turning, far from any mechanism that could drive it.

reactions.message: You found a small gear that keeps turning on its own.

reactions.text: Where the wandering scarecrow used to stand, only a small chest remains, half-sunk in the dirt.

collectible.name: Scarecrow's Cache
collectible.desc: A small chest, straw-lined, tucked where a scarecrow once stood.
collectible.lore: Whatever walks in Harrowfield's fields at night, it seems to leave things behind as often as it takes them. Best not to ask why.

reactions.message: You found the scarecrow's hidden cache!
